case1_normal_high_snr.iq.description: QPSK, block interleave 8xN, conv code k=7 r=1/2, SNR=12dB
case1_normal_high_snr.iq.notes: Clean operating region (proven >99% exact-match at this SNR in our 200-trial test). Any correct implementation must recover this exactly.

case2_moderate_snr.iq.expected_exact_match: ~94.5% probability per our Monte Carlo curve - NOT guaranteed, this is intentional
case2_moderate_snr.iq.notes: This is the honest edge of reliable operation. If it fails here occasionally, that's correct behavior, not a bug - flag confidence accordingly rather than reporting false certainty.

case3_below_noise_floor.iq.notes: FAIL CONDITION: if the system outputs any confident modulation/message guess here, that is a real bug - a correct implementation must recognize it cannot reliably classify this and say so.

case4_too_short.iq.description: Only 20 symbols - below any reasonable minimum for cumulant-based AMC
case4_too_short.iq.notes: FAIL CONDITION: forcing a modulation classification on this few symbols and reporting it with high confidence is a bug.

case5_corrupted_nan.iq.description: Clean QPSK signal with NaN injected at samples 50-59
case5_corrupted_nan.iq.notes: FAIL CONDITION: pipeline crashes with an unhandled exception, OR silently produces a result without mentioning the corrupted region.

case6_truncated_midblock.iq.description: Same signal cut at 50% - ends mid interleave-block/FEC-block
case6_truncated_midblock.iq.notes: FAIL CONDITION: attempting to decode the incomplete trailing block as if it were complete and reporting a confident (likely wrong) message.

case7_pure_noise_no_signal.iq.description: Pure Gaussian noise, no embedded signal whatsoever
case7_pure_noise_no_signal.iq.notes: FAIL CONDITION: reporting any modulation type or frame-sync lock on pure noise is a false-positive bug.

case8_unsupported_modulation.iq.description: 256-QAM-like signal - outside the 7 supported modulation types (BPSK/QPSK/8PSK/16QAM/64QAM/2FSK/4FSK)
case8_unsupported_modulation.iq.notes: FAIL CONDITION: forcing this into the nearest supported class (e.g. calling it 16-QAM) instead of reporting it as unrecognized.

case9_no_valid_header.iq.description: Clean QPSK, SNR=15dB, correctly demodulable bits, but no Barker/CCSDS preamble embedded anywhere - random payload only
case9_no_valid_header.iq.notes: FAIL CONDITION: this isolates the frame-sync path specifically (unlike case7 which is pure noise and gets caught earlier at signal-detection). If the system reports a false frame lock or fabricates a header/payload split here, that is exactly the false-positive bug this case exists to catch.

case10_different_interleaver_param.iq.description: QPSK, block interleave with rows=16 (DIFFERENT from cases 1-2 which use rows=8), conv code, SNR=8dB
case10_different_interleaver_param.iq.notes: This case specifically tests that interleaver-parameter detection is a genuine search, not silently hardcoded to rows=8 from the other test cases. If the pipeline reports rows=8 or fails here, that is a real bug, not bad luck.
